refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: platformd-verifyd.service is a system service that verifies the presence of the calling user. On request it runs the platformd-verify PAM stack. On success it submits the result to platformd-trustd.service8 when that service is available. Completion of this best-effort submission does not affect the verification result. Requests may be made with verifyctl1.

The user verified is always the caller's own, taken from the peer credentials of the connection rather than from a claimed name. The target must be an active, local, logind-reported unlocked session owned by that user. An explicitly named session is never replaced by another session. If no session is named, the service uses the caller's eligible session. If the caller is not associated with a session, the service selects the only eligible session for the caller.
The service drives PAM and therefore runs privileged. It announces readiness through sd_notify3 and terminates cleanly on SIGTERM.

refsect1.title: The Varlink interface
refsect1.para: The service exposes a single varlink7 interface, io.platformd.Verify, on a AF_UNIX socket at /run/platformd-verifyd/io.platformd.Verify. Its one method, VerifyUser, takes the session to refresh and a human-readable reason, runs the PAM stack, and returns whether the user was verified together with the PAM service that ran. The reason is descriptive text supplied by the client. It is not a verified application identity. Authentication responses do not cross this interface.

The PAM conversation runs in a forked worker, so a factor that waits at the reader does not block the service. One verification runs for each user at a time, with a bounded number across the machine. A concurrent call for the same user is refused with Busy. The worker is terminated when its client disconnects, the target session becomes ineligible, or the service deadline expires.

NoSession is returned if no logind session can be resolved. AmbiguousSession is returned if more than one eligible session remains. SessionNotEligible is returned if an explicitly named session is not eligible. PromptUnavailable reports that a compatible password agent could not accept a prompt. VerificationTimedOut and VerificationCancelled report deadline and cancellation failures.

refsect1.title: Factors
refsect1.para: The factors offered are the auth lines of the platformd-verify PAM stack (/usr/lib/pam.d/platformd-verify, overridable under /etc/pam.d/). The vendor stack uses pam_fprintd.so. Administrators may configure other PAM authentication modules. The first successful module verifies presence.

PAM password and PIN prompts are sent to the per-user io.systemd.AskPassword Varlink service. Prompt caching is disabled. The target session must provide a compatible systemd password agent for an interactive prompt to succeed. The prompt identifies platformd-verifyd and labels the client-supplied request description. It does not assert an application identity or a trusted graphical origin. Replies are returned only to PAM and are erased after use. Informational and error messages are written to the journal without authentication responses.
The reported method names the PAM service, not the individual PAM module that accepted the authentication.
